title: Publishing Below-Threshold Triangle Counts under Local Weight Differential Privacy
topic: Social Aspects->Privacy-preserving Statistics and Machine Learning
claim: Our smooth unbiased estimator achieves the lowest error across privacy budgets, graph sizes and thresholds, outperforming global and biased alternatives.
layout: 3 line-plot panels in a row, shared top legend, log-scale y-axes
description: A single wide strip of three small line plots sharing a legend at the top that lists five methods: smooth-unbiased (blue circles), baseline (red squares), global-unbiased (orange open circles), global-biased (green open squares) and smooth-biased (maroon diamonds). The y-axis in each panel is relative error on a log scale. Panel (a) varies the privacy parameter epsilon from 0 to 4. Error falls steeply, and the blue curve is lowest. Panel (b) varies the triangle count |Δ| in units of 10^6. The blue curve keeps decreasing, the biased variants stay flat near 10^-2, and the baseline stays roughly flat. Panel (c) varies the threshold lambda up to about 60. All curves drop quickly and then flatten. The red baseline and blue curve are lowest, and the orange curve plateaus highest. Marker shapes and bright colors identify each method.
caption: Relative error across all methods under different settings for the input graph ML-Tele-278: (a) as a function of the privacy parameter ε, (b) as a function of the number triangles |∆|, (c) as a function of the threshold λ.
abstract: We propose an algorithm for counting below-threshold triangles in weighted graphs under local weight differential privacy. While prior work has largely focused on unweighted graphs, edge weights are intrinsic to many real-world networks. We consider the setting in which the graph topology is publicly known and privacy is required only for the contribution of an individual to incident edge weights, capturing practical scenarios such as road and telecommunication networks. Our method uses two rounds of communication. In the first round, each node releases privatized information about its incident edge weights under local weight differential privacy. In the second round, nodes locally count below-threshold triangles using this privatized information; we introduce both biased and unbiased variants of the estimator. We further develop two refinements: (i) a pre-computation step that reduces covariance and thus lowers expected error, and (ii) an efficient procedure for computing smooth sensitivity, which substantially reduces running time relative to a straightforward implementation. Finally, we present experimental results that quantify the trade-offs between the biased and unbiased variants and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed improvements.
